assessment.body:
## Verdict

agent_supports: yes; daemon_capability: full; driver_capability: ready.

## Reasoning

**Agent.** Muse's runtime carries a real, per-call auto-classifier that decides whether a tool call needs review at all, distinct from muse's separate LLM-judge review mechanism. The discriminator lives in the task's `side_effect_intent.policy_decision` field (muse-format-spec.md §4): a plain, single-purpose read-only bash command (the confirmed example is `bash "ls -la"`) gets `policy_decision:"allow:policy"` and never opens a `kind:"approval"` record at all -- "executed with no wait". This is NOT a blanket bypass: the SAME session/profile, on a compound multi-step command (`cd /Users/ingo/projects/irrlicht && for d in ...`), instead opened the full `kind:"approval"` `requested -> automated_review_started -> automated_review_completed -> decision_applied` flow (muse-format-spec.md §5, session `01a09c71-ab1c-...`) -- proving the policy layer genuinely discriminates by command shape rather than pre-approving everything, the same contrastive-evidence shape the copilot 2-11 sibling cell used (cat auto-approved vs. echo>file gated) to rule out a vacuous "nothing ever prompts" recording.

**Daemon.** core/adapters/inbound/agents/muse/parser.go sources `waiting` exclusively from a `kind:"approval"` `requested`/`decision_applied` pair: parseApprovalRequested (parser.go:570-578) sets `PermissionRequestIDs` (-> `TranscriptPermissionPending`=true, state_classifier.go:152-156, rule `transcript_permission_prompt` -> waiting) and parseApprovalDecisionApplied (parser.go:583-591) clears it. A policy-fast-tracked call (`allow:policy`) never emits a `kind:"approval"` record of any kind, so `TranscriptPermissionPending` is never set for it and rule `transcript_permission_prompt` cannot fire -- waiting is structurally unreachable for this call, the same argument copilot's 2-11 cell makes for its own five-rule enumeration. Tool-call open/close for the bash call itself comes from the same `assistant_tool_calls_committed`/`tool_result_batch_committed` pair 2-2 already exercises (parser.go:445-484), so the working span is populated normally; turn boundaries come from `run.started`/`run.terminal` (parser.go:308-365) exactly as in every other muse cell.

## Establishing the three classifications and which the daemon can tell apart

Three distinct on-disk classifications exist for a muse tool call (muse-format-spec.md §4-5):

1. **Policy fast-track** -- `side_effect_intent.policy_decision:"allow:policy"`. No `kind:"approval"` record at all. Daemon: never enters waiting (this cell).
2. **LLM-judge auto-decision** -- a full `kind:"approval"` `requested -> automated_review_started -> automated_review_completed -> decision_applied` flow, with `decision_applied.decision_source.kind:"llm_judge"` -- the ONLY `decision_source.kind` ever observed in the 14-session corpus (muse-format-spec.md §5). Daemon: DOES enter waiting -- `TranscriptPermissionPending` flips true the instant `requested` is parsed and stays true until `decision_applied`, with no duration floor or debounce in state_classifier.go's rule. This is true regardless of how many milliseconds elapse between the two records; the daemon has no notion of "resolved so fast it doesn't count."
3. **Escalation to a human** -- never observed on disk (muse-format-spec.md §5/§12 gap list; confirmed again for this assessment by re-reading the same corpus). If it exists, parseApprovalDecisionApplied (parser.go:583-591) reads only `pending_action_id` -- it never inspects `decision`, `policy_result`, or `decision_source` -- so a hypothetical human-answered approval would be BYTE-IDENTICAL, daemon-side, to case 2. Classes 2 and 3 are therefore NOT distinguishable by irrlicht today; only class 1 vs. {2,3} is.

Consequence for THIS scenario: muse's LLM-judge auto-decision (class 2), despite being fully automated with no human ever involved, is NOT the mechanism that satisfies "no transition to waiting at any point" -- it produces a genuine, real waiting blip in the daemon, identical in shape to a slow human answer. Only class 1 (policy fast-track) satisfies the scenario's literal acceptance criterion for muse. This makes muse's mapping of "auto-classified, no prompt" narrower than Claude Code's Auto Mode (where the classifier's OWN decision, whatever it is, either fires a hook or doesn't) or Copilot's classifier (same shape) -- muse's judge-mediated "automatic" path still counts as blocking from the state machine's perspective, and only the policy pre-filter genuinely never blocks.

**Driver.** replaydata/agents/muse/driver-interactive.sh's DRIVE_ELICITS lists send, slash, wait_turn, sleep, exit_clean as implemented (same citation as the 2-2 cell, driver-interactive.sh:139,441-461); this recipe needs only send + wait_turn + sleep.

## Vacuous-pass condition (load-bearing)

Under what condition would this cell pass while proving nothing? Two distinct risks, both addressed:

1. If the recipe's command instead routed through the LLM-judge review flow (class 2) -- even though no human ever sees anything -- the daemon would show a real `working -> waiting -> working` blip and the cell would (correctly) FAIL the no-waiting invariant, for a reason that has nothing to do with a driver or daemon defect: it would just mean the chosen command wasn't policy-fast-tracked. The recipe therefore uses a plain, single-purpose, no-compound-syntax bash command (`echo hello`, the exact wording the scenario description itself proposes and the one claudecode's own 2-11 sibling recipe uses) rather than a multi-step/compound one -- but `echo hello` itself has NOT been directly observed getting `allow:policy` in the muse corpus (only `ls -la` has, muse-format-spec.md §4); this is a reasoned inference (single trivial no-side-effect command, same shape class as the confirmed `ls -la` example) rather than a confirmed fact, which is why confidence sits at 0.78 rather than 2-2's 0.82 and why record's live probe is load-bearing here, not just corroborating.
2. If this cell's recording turned out to be byte-mechanically identical to 2-2's (same command, same daemon code path) it would prove nothing NEW about the daemon. Using `echo hello` instead of 2-2's `ls -la` keeps the fixtures distinct even though both exercise the identical parser code path (assistant_tool_calls_committed/tool_result_batch_committed with no approval record) -- that overlap is expected and correct (the SAME daemon capability legitimately backs both scenarios), not a defect to engineer around.

**Recording prerequisite, named as a precondition below**: this machine's muse install runs the `:auto-review` permission profile (confirmed via `runtime.session.permission_profile_committed` naming `"id": ":auto-review"`, muse-format-spec.md §5) -- a different profile could route even trivial commands through review, or skip review entirely for everything, which would either falsify or trivialize this cell. Re-probe this at record time.
caveats: Not yet recorded for this scenario -- grounded in the built adapter's code, its own unit tests (parser_test.go:270 TestParseLine_ToolCall_OpenAndClose_PairByCallID; parser_test.go:323,335 TestParseLine_ApprovalRequested_OpensPermission / TestParseLine_ApprovalDecisionApplied_ClosesPermission), and the muse-format-spec.md live corpus (including the already-recorded 2-2 sibling's LIVE-CONFIRMED note that `ls -la` really does classify allow:policy on this machine) -- not a live run of THIS scenario's exact recipe; record promotes it from provisional to settled.

PROVISIONAL command classification: the recipe uses `echo hello` (the scenario description's own suggested example, and the literal command claudecode's sibling 2-11 recipe uses), reasoned by analogy to the confirmed `ls -la` -> allow:policy example (muse-format-spec.md §4) but never itself directly observed on this muse install. If `echo hello` unexpectedly opens a kind:"approval" record, the recording fails loudly (a real waiting transition appears) rather than silently -- the fix would be to fall back to the confirmed `ls -la` shape, at the cost of duplicating 2-2's exact fixture.

Load-bearing environment property: this machine's muse install runs the `:auto-review` permission profile (muse-format-spec.md §5, runtime.session.permission_profile_committed id ":auto-review"). A different profile configuration could change which commands get policy-fast-tracked vs. reviewed, or remove the policy fast-track entirely -- re-probe at record time.

Muse's LLM-judge auto-decision path (decision_source.kind:"llm_judge", the only value ever observed) is DAEMON-INDISTINGUISHABLE from a hypothetical human-answered approval -- parseApprovalDecisionApplied (parser.go:583-591) reads only pending_action_id, never decision_source. Both would show as a genuine waiting->working arc. No human-answered example has ever been captured (muse-format-spec.md §12 gap list) so this is an architectural observation about the parser's current scope, not a confirmed present-day bug -- recorded here as the open item this assessment was asked to establish, not to settle.

automated_review_started/automated_review_completed (the LLM-judge's own review-lifecycle bookkeeping, only relevant on the class-2 approval-flow path this cell's recipe deliberately avoids) are explicitly skipped by the parser's default arm (parseApprovalEvent, parser.go:554-564) -- automated_review_completed carries the judge's own real usage/token figures for the review call itself, which the parser does not currently read into any metric. This does not affect this cell (its tokens_nonzero observation comes from the main turn's own model_completed record, unaffected by the judge path), but is a recorded open item on the sibling approval-flow scenario (2.19 tool-gate-permission-prompt, not yet assessed for muse), not something this cell settles.

Same vacuous-pass mechanism already found and fixed in the 2-2/turn-end-terminal-text sibling cells during the #1960 record pass applies here too: muse spawns goal-reminder/verify-reminder subagents that go straight to working (skipping ready) before the parent session's own turn starts, and one of those subagents' own read-only arc can satisfy an unpinned ready->working->ready-with-no-waiting shape on its own. turn_start/turn_end are pinned to same_session_as:session_birth below for exactly this reason.

cost_nonzero is asserted false, matching every other muse cell: muse-spark-1.3-contributor has no litellm pricing/alias entry (core/pkg/capacity has zero hits for muse/spark; the daemon logs 'no pricing for model ... cost will be 0' on every recording, per the 2-2 sibling's LIVE-CONFIRMED note).
